thesis_summary.thesis: Circle Internet Group, Inc. is the issuer of **USDC**, a dollar-backed stablecoin used for payments, trading, and settlement on public blockchains and inside bank and fintech apps. **[Fact]** The company went public on the NYSE (**CRCL**) in **June 2025** and files as a single reportable segment. **[Fact]** Revenue is driven mainly by interest earned on segregated reserves backing USDC in circulation, plus a smaller and faster-growing **platform services** line (mint/redeem, treasury, and developer APIs). **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$2.75 billion** (up **64%** versus last year), net income **$69.5 million**, and stockholders' equity **$3.33 billion**. **[Fact]** Segregated stablecoin reserves were **$75.1 billion** at December 31, 2025, up from **$43.9 billion** a year earlier.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The stock may trade as a levered bet on USDC supply growth and short-term reserve yields while understating how thin normalized owner cash is relative to a **~$12.7 billion** equity market cap at **$80.28**. **[Inference]** FY2025 **operating profit fell to $96.4 million** from **$167 million** in 2024 even as reserve balances grew, because higher operating spend (compliance, distribution, stock compensation, and public-company costs) consumed much of the reserve-yield uplift. **[Inference]** Generalists may treat Circle like a regulated money-market fund wrapper, but shareholders own the franchise margin on float, not the **$75 billion** of segregated reserves. **[Inference]** Conversely, bears may underweight the durability of USDC's compliance-first positioning if U.S. stablecoin legislation clarifies issuer rules. Return here is **earnings power at price**, not a dated catalyst (no HK predictive attribute in base).
